definitions.explanation: A person sent to propagate a religion, especially Christianity, in a foreign country or region. Historically significant in the context of European contact with Japan.

examples.japanese: {宣教師|せんきょうし}が{来日|らいにち}した。
フランシスコ・ザビエルは{日本|にほん}に{初|はじ}めて{来|き}た{宣教師|せんきょうし}の{一人|ひとり}だ。
examples.english: Francisco Xavier was one of the first missionaries to come to Japan.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}にはキリスト{教|きょう}が{禁止|きんし}され、{宣教師|せんきょうし}は{国外|こくがい}に{追放|ついほう}された。
examples.english: During the Edo period, Christianity was banned and missionaries were expelled from the country.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{宣教|せんきょう} (proselytization, missionary work) + {師|し} (master, teacher, practitioner).

CULTURAL NOTE:
{宣教師|せんきょうし} is closely associated with the history of Christianity in Japan. The first European missionaries arrived in the 16th century during the {戦国|せんごく}{時代|じだい} (Warring States period). The subsequent {禁教|きんきょう}{令|れい} (ban on Christianity) during the {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい} is a major historical topic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- キリスト{教|きょう}の{宣教師|せんきょうし}: Christian missionary
- {宣教師|せんきょうし}を{派遣|はけん}する: to send missionaries
- {宣教師|せんきょうし}{活動|かつどう}: missionary activities
